strategy.summary: Reproduce gh-22346/gh-16352 in a from-source NumPy build of the buggy commit 6a8599103202 with the developer's two test-file edits applied. The new test test_cast_overflow_safe_unit_conversion in test_datetime.py should fail on the buggy build (astype wraps silently, so pytest.raises reports DID NOT RAISE) and pass on the fixed build (OverflowError with 'Overflow' in the message). test_time_to_time is not part of the transition because its edit swallows OverflowError and breaks, so it passes on both builds.

system_packages: a C/C++ compiler toolchain (gcc or clang)
build_commands: git apply the test diff onto numpy/_core/tests/test_datetime.py and numpy/_core/tests/test_casting_unittests.py
python -m pip install -r requirements/build_requirements.txt (or the build-system.requires list from pyproject.toml)
python -m pip install --no-build-isolation -e . (compiles dtype_transfer.c and datetime.c, which hold the behaviour under test)
git checkout <fixed PR head or merge commit for #31085>, then rebuild with the same -e install and rerun the same pytest command

strategy.reproducing_test: numpy/_core/tests/test_datetime.py::test_cast_overflow_safe_unit_conversion (method in the datetime cast test class; selected via -k)
strategy.success_criterion: Buggy revision: test_cast_overflow_safe_unit_conversion FAILS at its first pytest.raises(OverflowError) block (the datetime64[h] to datetime64[ns] upconversion of 2367-12-31 12:00), because astype returns a wrapped value and no exception is raised. Fixed revision: test_cast_overflow_safe_unit_conversion PASSES, with every OverflowError raised and matching 'Overflow', every boundary value (9223372036 s OK, 9223372037 s raises) correct, and the NaT and num!=1 cases correct. test_time_to_time passes on both revisions and does not contribute to the transition.
strategy.numerical_probe: python -c "import numpy as np; np.datetime64(np.iinfo(np.int64).min + 1, 's').astype('M8[m]')" (buggy: exits 0 with no exception; fixed: raises OverflowError, exit status non-zero)
risks: Only a from-source build of the C casting code shows the defect; a prebuilt numpy wheel of either revision will not reproduce it, so the build step is mandatory.

The test asserts match='Overflow', so the fixed build must raise an OverflowError whose message contains 'Overflow'; the evidence does not state the exact message text, so a mismatch would fail the fixed run too.

Signed int64 multiplication is undefined behaviour in C. The buggy wrap was observed in an optimised build; a build with -fwrapv or a different optimisation level could change how the buggy value appears, though the test should still fail on the buggy build because no exception is raised. A UBSan build would flag the buggy code but is not needed for the transition.

The test file uses an arbitrary-precision pytest.raises across many cases, so the first failing assertion on the buggy build is the gh-16352 upconversion block, not the gh-22346 downconversion. The transition does not depend on which block fails first.
The fixed commit hash is not given in the context. Use the PR head or merge commit for #31085 and confirm that it is the revision carrying _datetime_scale_with_overflow_check.
Test_time_to_time now catches OverflowError and breaks, so it may not verify values for extreme inputs. It is not a reliable transition signal.
Exact boundary behaviour (9223372036 s safe, 9223372037 s overflows) appears only in a discussion comment and in the new test; no separate source confirms it.
The environment's test_commands entry, python -c 'import numpy; numpy.test()', runs the whole suite and does not select the relevant test, so it is not used here.

No Python version, pytest version or hypothesis version is documented or era-constrained. The plan uses the latest versions that install with the repository's build requirements and records that choice here; if collection fails with a newer hypothesis, pin it to the version that the repository's requirements files specify.
The environment's dependency entries are marked numerically_relevant false, so pytest and hypothesis are chosen without numerical constraints.

oracle.reference_source: issue#22346 and the developer test expectations (OverflowError with 'Overflow' in the message)
oracle.why: The defect is a silent wrong value, and the fix converts it to an exception. The oracle is the exception type and message, with no numerical tolerance involved.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy build the first pytest.raises(OverflowError, match='Overflow') block, for arr.astype('datetime64[ns]') on 2367-12-31 12:00 in datetime64[h], reports DID NOT RAISE, because int64 multiplication wraps and astype returns a wrong date without an exception.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed build every OverflowError block raises with 'Overflow' in the message, the boundary values behave as specified, NaT passes through, the num!=1 path is correct, and the valid-conversion asserts hold.
